original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Does the published E7 bit-lane iterator emit exactly the weight-at-most-12 words of the 27-dimensional kernel, as an independent half-split census and the predecessor receipt both count them?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a new measured speedup. PR #5729 already published the bit-lane speedup and was archived without an independent replay. The revision-8 verification row says that faster output is not equivalent coverage until checked. This package checks that coverage on the full E7 kernel and does not add another optimization.
bottleneck_link: A faster E7 exhaustion is useful for deletion and decoder checks only if it still returns every minimum-weight word. This comparison certifies that iterator on the pinned kernel. It does not change a supplier bill or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after one full-kernel set comparison of the published engine against two independent splits. Do not remeasure the timing claim, rerun reflection orbits, or install the engine into another consumer.
evidence: Two half-splits agree on 1639 words of weight at most 12: zero plus 1638 weight-12 words, with no lighter nonzero word, over all 134217728 codewords. low_weight_words at batch sizes 16 and 8 returns that same set. The counts match source/RESULT.json. A dropped support and an injected weight-11 word fail.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Do the two predecessor orbit hashes still partition this independently recovered support set?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The iterator check does not rerun reflections or quadratic ranks, so the archived classification receipt is not re-certified.
open_questions.first_step: Apply the frozen reflection permutations in source/verify.py to this support set and compare both orbit hashes with source/RESULT.json.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not recompute the 63 reflection maps.

open_questions.question: Does the same set equality hold for one other deletion or decoder code named by the bit-lane proof?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The published open question asks to bind another consumer before claiming that the iterator is coverage-preserving outside E7.
open_questions.first_step: Name that code's generators, width and weight bound, then run this half-split against low_weight_words on that basis alone.
open_questions.blocked_by: No second consumer is pinned here.
